title: slo-credit-budgeting-and-regional-throttle-backstop
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce region-level SLO credit bucket with soft throttling and a control-plane backstop to prevent cross-region cascade failures. Improves availability during bursty traffic and provides clearer observability for throttled requests.
description: Summary: Implements a region-scoped SLO credit bucket and an emergency control-plane throttle backstop. This PR adds a token-bucket style accounting layer that tracks SLO credit consumption per region and a control-plane backstop that enforces conservative throttles when regional failures risk cascading. Motivation: Recent incidents showed that a noisy region could consume cross-region capacity via retries and fallback traffic, violating global SLOs. Instead of immediate global shedding, we now budget per-region SLO credits and automatically deprioritize non-critical routes once a region's credits are exhausted. Design highlights: - SLO credit bucket: region -> token bucket with refill rate derived from configured SLOs (slo_engine/config). Tokens are consumed by request class (critical, standard, best_effort). - Soft throttle policy: when tokens < threshold, requests in 'best_effort' are admitted probabilistically (p = tokens/threshold) and annotated with reasoncode. - Control-plane backstop: if regional error rate + latency exceeds configured emergency thresholds, the control plane enforces a short-term conservative cap across all non-critical tails for that region and triggers an alert. - Observability: new metrics (region.slo_tokens, region.slo_burn_rate, region.throttle_events) and traces include slo_token_state tags. Checklist: - [x] SLO token bucket implementation - [x] Soft admission/rejection policy - [x] Control-plane backstop + alerts - [x] Unit tests for token accounting and admission policy - [x] Integration test that simulates a noisy region and verifies downstream fallbacks - [x] Docs: config knobs and recommended defaults (docs/ops/slo-buckets.md) Commits (high-level): - feat(slo): add region token bucket and refill logic - feat(control-plane): add emergency throttle backstop and alerting hook - perf(runtime): optimize admission fast-path to avoid heap allocations under steady state - test: add integration scenario for cross-region noisy neighbor - docs: add operations guidance and config examples Files/areas touched (high level): - runtime/slo/bucket.go (new): token bucket and accounting - runtime/slo/admission.go: admission policy and request annotator - controlplane/throttle_manager.go: backstop enforcement + alerting hook - api/diagnostics/metrics.go: new metrics exports - docs/ops/slo-buckets.md: operator guidance - tests/integration/noisy_region_test.go: scenario test - sdk/ts/examples/slo-config.ts: example config for TS SDK Small snippet (admission fast-path): "if request.Class == 'best_effort' && tokens < softThreshold { if rand.Float64() > float64(tokens)/float64(softThreshold) { return reject(ReasonThrottleSLO) } } // annotate and continue" Migration notes: default behavior is off. Cluster operators must opt in by adding slo_buckets under runtime config; recommended defaults are included in docs. Backwards compatibility: request headers and APIs unchanged; only internal routing/annotations added. Review conversation (selected highlights): - Jordan Li (reviewer): "Can we make the softThreshold configurable per-route? In traffic-heavy customers we still want some routes to have higher headroom." - Aisha (author): "Added per-route override support in admission.go and documented the fallback order (route -> service -> region). See commit feat(slo): add per-route overrides." - Maya Chen: "Control-plane backstop looks good; please add an integration test that simulates retry storms from failing region to ensure we don't amplify load." - Aisha: "Added tests/integration/noisy_region_test.go that runs a simulated retry loop and asserts throttle_events increase and overall global error budget stays within bounds." - Ethan Park: "CI flagged a flaky test (runtime/kvcache_test). I suspect a timing assumption. Can you make the test less time-sensitive?" - Aisha: "Adjusted test to use a deterministic clock in test harness; reran CI." CI history: First run: lint/pass, unit tests/pass, integration/fail (flaky kv cache timing). I fixed tests to use deterministic clock and re-ran: all checks passed. Observability after merge: dashboards updated to include new metrics under 'SRE/SLO Buckets' and alert rules added to staging by ops. Rollout plan: - Canary: enable region SLO buckets in 10% of production regions for 24h - Telemetry: monitor region.slo_burn_rate and region.throttle_events; auto-roll-back if we see >5% increase in P95 latency for critical routes in canary regions - Gradual rollout to 100% after 72h of stable telemetry Merge notes: squashed into one commit and merged to main after approvals from Jordan and Maya. No manual migration required; ops should review docs/ops/slo-buckets.md for tuning knobs. Related: ENG-7123 (design doc), SUP-4551 (customer impact report that motivated emergency backstop).
